subject: Aurum renewal bakeoff and capacity acceleration — next steps
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@aurum.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tellis@aurum.ai>, procurement@aurum.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aurum renewal — planned bakeoff and scope / urgency

Hi Jonas / Laura,

Thanks again for the call last week. Aurum is coming up on renewal in Q1 and the exec team has asked us to run a side-by-side bakeoff with a vendor who claims a 30% cost improvement on our inference spend. They want demonstration of throughput at 2x current sustained qps on our 4k token average, and a clear migration path for an in-production model set.

To be transparent: Finance is pushing a short window for proofs — they want results and an economic proposal within 10 business days. Tom (cc) is leading the technical evaluation; procurement is on the timeline.

Ask: can Redwood run a timeboxed benchmark on our representative workload this week? We can share sample traces and a trimmed model set. Also need a concise save plan that addresses:
- Proof of parity (latency and quality) for the top 3 models
- Cost/throughput path for 2x qps on our current traffic profile
- Operational migration notes (KV cache, padding, quantization tradeoffs)

I attached the workload readme.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Ops, Aurum.ai
Attachments: aurum-bench-readme.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@aurum.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurum renewal — planned bakeoff and scope / urgency

Samira — thanks for the clarity and the readme. We take timeboxes seriously and can run a focused validation sprint this week. High-level plan we propose:

1) Intake (today): ingest your traces + model tarball, confirm sequence length distribution, tokenization parity.
2) Quick-run (24–48 hrs): 1:1 latency tests on your 3 top models at target 4k token avg; measure p50/p90/p99 and quality via your eval harness.
3) Load-fold (48–72 hrs): scale to 2x qps using Redwood Dedicated staging pool and capture throughput/OSP metrics.
4) Deliverable (end of timebox): side-by-side report, cost delta by token, recommended config (batching/quantization/profile) and an executable rollback plan.

We can include a limited SLA uplift and a short-term pilot discount to make switching economically unattractive. I'll get Ben to scope the quantization/ops tradeoffs; Laura will lead commercial & SLA framing.

One ask on your side: please provide a small set of golden prompts (100–200) and the evaluation script so we can run an apples-to-apples quality comparison.

I'll schedule a 30-min kickoff at 1pm PT unless you prefer another time.

Jonas Weber
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@aurum.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurum renewal — planned bakeoff and scope / urgency

Quick technical note from the infra side — copying the proposed benchmark config we typically use for high-sequence workloads:

- Instance profile: 4x A100-equivalent (dedicated) with 96GB KV cache headroom
- Runtime knobs: continuous batching window = 6ms, dynamic shard routing to keep p99 tails below 300ms for 4k tokens
- Quantization: run INT8-RT and FP16 parity pass; we expect ~1.6–1.9x token throughput on INT8 without measurable quality drop for transformer44 variants, but we need your eval set to confirm.
- Caching: prefix/KV hot-cache population using first-10k sessions; we’ll show delta versus cold-state.

Attachments: trial-configs.zip (includes the cluster JSON and runbook).

I’ll spin up the staging cluster once Samira shares the sample traces and the model artifacts (or access to an S3 bucket). If the customer needs logs for procurement / security — we can produce an audit package and a SOC-summary extract for the pilot.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira@aurum.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aurum renewal — planned bakeoff and scope / urgency

Appreciate the quick response — that plan looks good. Tom sent the golden prompts and model artifacts to S3 (bucket aurum-eval-2026, I shared an access token to jonas.weber@redwood.com).

Two quick clarifications before kickoff:
1) Our procurement lead needs a succinct SLA uplift bullet to include in the RFP addendum — can Laura draft a one-paragraph SLA uplift and list of demo metrics?
2) If the 2x qps target requires transient overprovisioning, we need clear monthly cost delta and a recommended intermediate commitment (e.g., 3-month reserved burst pool).

We’re ready to start on the ingest. Kickoff at 1pm PT works for us — see you then.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of ML Ops, Aurum.ai
